findings.title: simctl read now runs synchronously in EnsureReady with no deadline of its own
findings.body: The old code recorded boots in a goroutine bounded by `context.WithTimeout(p.life, 30*time.Second)`. `p.currentBoots(ctx)` now runs `xcrun simctl list devices` inline, while `EnsureReady` holds `p.startMu`, so every concurrent caller waits behind it. Its only bound is the caller's ctx (`p.run` at provider.go:126 adds no timeout). A wedged CoreSimulator can hang `simctl list`, and that would block hub startup. The failure path does degrade to nil, but only after ctx ends. Wrapping this one call in a short `context.WithTimeout` (about 15–30s, like the old goroutine) would keep the old bound. The read has to happen before `startHub`, so it cannot go back to a goroutine.

findings.title: TestHubStartRecordsEverySimulatorsBoot no longer exercises the hub-start wiring
findings.body: The test used to call `recordBoots`. It now calls `currentBoots` and `storeBootsLocked` by hand, so it only tests that the two helpers compose. It would still pass if `EnsureReady` stopped calling them, or called them after `startHub`, which is the ordering this PR changes. `EnsureReady` has no test for 'boots are read before the hub starts and stored once it is installed'. The test name and its comment ('A hub's helpers belong to the boots its simulators were on when it started') claim more than it checks. Either drive `EnsureReady` with fake `lookPath`/`run` or rename the test to match what it does.
